Fit a Bayesian multilevel VAR network model

Source: R/bvar.R
bvar.Rd

The bvar function estimates the posterior distribution of the specified Bayesian (Multilevel) Vector Autoregression.

Usage

bvar(
  id_col,
  time_col,
  beep_col = NULL,
  y_cols,
  x_cols = NULL,
  center_x = FALSE,
  fe_interactions = NULL,
  re_interactions = NULL,
  re_cols = NULL,
  re_temporal = FALSE,
  K = 1,
  na_action = c("listwise"),
  data,
  family = c("bernoulli", "ordinal", "gaussian"),
  priors = set_priors(),
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 1000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  adapt_delta = NULL,
  max_treedepth = NULL,
  save_data = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

id_col

Character. Name of the subject/group identifier column.

time_col

Character scalar naming the time-index column in data. Its meaning depends on beep_col:

  • If beep_col = NULL (default), this column contains the scheduled occasion index for one sequence per subject. Values must be finite and integer-valued, with one unit representing one scheduled lag step. Indices must continue across the subject's sequence rather than restart each day. For lag k, the predecessor must have index time - k. No separate day or overnight boundary is inferred in this mode.

  • If beep_col names a column, time_col identifies the day or session. beep_col then contains finite integer-valued beep indices within each day/session, with one unit representing one scheduled lag step. Beep indices may restart in each day/session. For lag k, the predecessor must have index beep - k in the same subject and day/session.

Preserve the original scheduled labels when observations are missing. Rows without a complete, correctly spaced lag window are excluded as responses from the likelihood; their observed outcomes may still be used as predictors for later eligible responses.

beep_col

NULL (default), or a character scalar naming the scheduled occasion index within each day/session, specified in the time_col column. If NULL, time_col itself supplies the occasion index for one sequence per subject, and no day/session splitting is performed. If supplied, time_col must identify the day/session and this column must contain finite integer-valued beep indices, with one unit representing one scheduled lag step. Beep indices may restart in each day/session. For lag k, the predecessor must have index beep - k in the same subject and day/session.

y_cols

Character vector. Names of the outcome columns.

x_cols

Character vector or NULL. Names of the covariate columns.

center_x

Logical. Grand-mean centre covariates before fitting? Default FALSE.

fe_interactions

List or NULL. Fixed-effect interaction terms to add to the design matrix. Each element is a character vector of column names to interact, or c("lag", "x") to interact all lag columns with a covariate.

re_interactions

List or NULL. Random-effect interaction terms.

re_cols

Character vector. Columns from X and/or "Intercept" to include as random slopes.

re_temporal

Logical. Include random slopes on lag predictors? Default FALSE.

K

Integer. AR order. Default 1.

na_action

Character. Missing-data strategy; currently only "listwise".

data

Data frame in long format.

family

Character scalar or vector. Observation model per node. A scalar is recycled to all y_cols. A vector of length length(y_cols) (named or positional) specifies per-node families. Valid values: "bernoulli", "ordinal", "gaussian".

priors

A bvarnet_priors object from set_priors(). Defaults to set_priors() (package defaults).

iter

Integer. Number of post-warmup iterations per chain. Default 4000.

warmup

Integer. Number of warmup iterations per chain. Default 1000.

chains

Integer. Number of MCMC chains. Default 4.

cores

Integer. Number of chains to run in parallel. Default 1.

seed

Integer or NULL. RNG seed.

adapt_delta

Numeric in (0, 1). Target average proposal acceptance probability during warmup adaptation. Higher values (e.g., 0.95–0.99) reduce divergences at the cost of slower sampling. Default NULL (CmdStan default of 0.8).

max_treedepth

Integer. Maximum depth of the NUTS binary tree. Increasing this allows the sampler to take more leapfrog steps per iteration, which can help with difficult posteriors (e.g., funnels in hierarchical logistic models) but increases computation. Default NULL (CmdStan default of 10).

save_data

Logical. Keep the Stan data used for estimation in the returned object's standata slot? Default TRUE. Set to FALSE to remove these data from the fitted model before saving or sharing it, for example when working with sensitive data. Model dimensions, variable labels, posterior draws and effective priors are retained; this option does not anonymize posterior results.

...

Additional named arguments forwarded to the CmdStanR $sample() method, e.g. init, refresh, thin, step_size, or show_messages. See ?cmdstanr::"model-method-sample" for the full list. Arguments that bvar() sets itself (data, seed, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, chains, parallel_chains, adapt_delta, max_treedepth, and CmdStanR's deprecated aliases for them) are rejected with an error; use the corresponding bvar() argument instead.

Value

A bvarnet object (a named list) with slots: draws, convergence, diagnostics, timing, metadata, return_codes, family, model_info, priors, and priors_effective. The standata slot contains the estimation data when save_data = TRUE (default) and is NULL when save_data = FALSE. The model_info slot retains only dimensions and variable/interaction labels needed for summaries and parameter extraction. No additional data frame is stored.

Scheduled time and missing observations

Index columns identify eligible transitions; they do not automatically add time or day effects as covariates. A daily series with one observation per day can use time_col = "day" alone: consecutive days are ordinary lag steps. With multiple observations per day, supply both day and beep columns to exclude overnight transitions. Day/session labels may be numeric, character, factor or Date; occasion indices must be numeric integers. Retained keys must be unique within subject (and day/session when supplied), with no missing keys.

Only complete lag windows enter the likelihood. For indices 1, 2, 4, 5, a VAR(1) uses 1 -> 2 and 4 -> 5, excluding 2 -> 4. With day/beep indices, day 1 beep 5 never predicts day 2 beep 1, while day 2 beep 1 can predict day 2 beep 2. Subject random effects remain shared across that subject's days. Occasion-level listwise deletion is applied to all selected outcomes and covariates before constructing lags. This is not a general correction for missingness under MAR or MNAR.

The former skip_lag argument and zero-filled gap likelihood were removed because they could bias temporal and non-temporal parameters. Passing the removed argument is an error. Fits may use fewer responses and give different estimates than the former default.

Internal predictor centering

Stan samples intercepts (Gaussian/Bernoulli) or thresholds (ordinal) using centered completed fixed-effect and lag columns. Reported beta, kappa, priors and Bayes-factor hypotheses retain the reference of the public design produced with the requested center_x setting. Random-effect designs and priors are unchanged. This coordinate change can improve sampling, but does not guarantee a speed improvement.

Requested versus effective priors

priors holds the priors as you specified them. priors_effective holds the priors Stan actually sampled under: one bvarnet_priors object per outcome. The two differ for Gaussian outcomes left at their default priors, where intercept, beta and sigma scales are multiplied by the outcome SD so that unit-scale defaults stay weakly informative on the raw data scale. User-supplied priors are never rescaled.

Bayes factors (bf_table) divide by priors_effective, as the Savage-Dickey density ratio requires. Note that the joint path (family a single value) scales every outcome by the mean SD across outcomes, whereas the nodewise path (mixed family) scales each outcome by its own SD, so the same data can imply slightly different effective priors depending on which path runs.

See also

bvarnet_setup_models, which must be run once before the first bvar() call to set up the required Stan models (either by downloading precompiled binaries or compiling them locally).

Examples

# Scheduled indices retain missing occasions rather than compressing time.
single_index <- data.frame(id = 1, occasion = c(1, 2, 4, 5), y = c(1, 2, 3, 4))
# time_col = "occasion": transitions 1 -> 2 and 4 -> 5 are eligible.
day_beep <- data.frame(id = 1, day = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2),
                       beep = c(1, 2, 4, 1, 2), y = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
# time_col = "day", beep_col = "beep": only within-day beeps 1 -> 2.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Run bvar on studentlife data
data(studentlife, package = "bvarnet")
fit <- bvar(
  id_col = "id",
  time_col = "day",
  y_cols = c("anxious", "calm", "conventional", "critical", "dependable"),
  re_temporal = TRUE,
  K = 1,
  data = studentlife,
  family = "ordinal",
  priors = set_priors(),
  seed = 1337)

summary(fit)
} # }
